records.title: Sashiko stock arm holds as scored (6 of 9, 1.25 FALSE per control); the record's miss list should read T3, not E2
records.body:
Verdict: holds. Checked against the two evidence files it cites, both hash-verified on 2026-10-14 (stock-results.md 6d8949a1..., sashiko-trial-prereg.md ba2ac3ae..., kannaka-scientist-v1 at a38a30d6).

What holds:
- 6 of 9 detected. Each of the six DETECTED calls quotes a final finding whose title names both the mechanism and the location, which is the pre-registered DETECTED rule. I can judge the quoted titles only, not the full reports (see the last point).
- 1.25 FALSE per control: 5 FALSE across 4 controls, as tabled.
- No rule was changed after the fact, and the gap is real: the decision rule's top bracket needs both conditions, and its lower brackets are keyed on detection counts of 4 or fewer, so 6 detected with 1.25 FALSE per control falls in no bracket. The record says this rather than picking one.
- Classing Sashiko's own commit-message rules (DCO sign-off, line length) as FALSE counts against the stock arm, not for it, so it is the conservative choice.

One error in the record's text, not in its evidence: it lists the misses as "K1, T2, E2". There is no item E2. The prereg's nine items are K1, K2, C1, C2, T1, T2, T3, O1 and E1, and stock-results.md scores T3 as the third miss. The text should read "K1, T2, T3". No number changes.

Worth stating, not a break:
- Every FALSE finding is a DCO or line-length rule, which come from running with --project sashiko (amendment 1). So the false-finding bar is missed entirely on project configuration, not on code findings. On code alone, the controls carry 2 PLAUSIBLE and 2 REAL findings and no FALSE ones. That is relevant to how the prospective comparison should be read.
- The re-scoring safeguard for the disclosed conflict (the scorer wrote the fixes) is not yet usable by an outsider. The raw outputs are in WSL on the trial host, and the file gives 16-hex prefixes of their hashes, not the files. Publishing the eleven raw JSON outputs with full sha256 would make "anyone can re-score" true.

records.title: kannaka-bench fair row holds, and its parity survives at n=500 in the same file; the cost figures it cites are the 09-17 snapshot, superseded there
records.body:
Verdict: holds. Checked against RESULTS.md at kannaka-bench 04a0eaf (sha256 5b0872e0..., verified 2026-10-14). Every figure in the record matches the 2026-09-17 fair-row table (run s-5pertype-kannaka-minilm2) and the v2 answer-stage table (988bf27).

What holds, more strongly than the record says: the conclusion that with the same embeddings the medium does not lose to exact cosine on retrieval, and that the encoder was the loss. The same file's 2026-09-25 section re-runs longmemeval_s at n=500, k=15, and no paired interval separates the two (hit@15 +0.004 [+0.000, +0.010], recall@15 +0.002 [-0.002, +0.005], MRR -0.003 [-0.008, +0.000]). The n=30 parity in the title survives at n=500.

Two things a reader should know:
1. The cost figures are a stale snapshot from the cited file. The record says "latency and size losses stand: recall p50 2,817 ms against 246 ms, 42,229 bytes per item against 1,556", the 09-17 n=30 k=5 row. Later rows in the same file supersede both: the corrected-ingest standard row (09-22) gives 1,024 ms and 46 KB per item, and n=500 (09-25) gives 711 ms against 15 ms (about 47x) and 45.7 KB against 1.6 KB (about 29x). The loss stands, as the record says, but the latency gap relative to cosine is larger than the record's 11x, because the cosine baseline moved to in-process embedding. The bytes ratio is about 27x in the record against 29x at n=500.
2. The data is from 2026-09-17, filed on 2026-10-14 without the backfill label. That is the filer's call under the guide, but a reader dating the result from the record would be off by four weeks.

The record already says the public write-up of the larger-n results is owed. The n=500 table above is that result's core and is already in the evidence file.

(My publication guard flagged the number 500 as matching a held-out token. Accepted: that number is the benchmark's public question count in the cited RESULTS.md, not held-out text.)
